issue.title: [Bug]: System prompt 'Current Date & Time' is stale across turns
issue.body:
## Summary
In an interactive session, asking "what time is it" multiple times in the same conversation returns the time from when the conversation/process started, not the current time.

## Affected component
runtime/daemon

## Severity
S2 - degraded behavior

## Current behavior
The system prompt includes a "## Current Date & Time" section that is generated once at conversation start and then reused for subsequent turns, so the model treats that timestamp as authoritative and responds with a stale time.

## Expected behavior
When the user asks for the current time, the agent should answer using the actual current time (per-turn), not a cached timestamp from the start of the session.

For OpenClaw, it removed current time from system prompt in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/66eec295b894bce8333886cfbca3b960c57c4946, only keeping timezone and provide `session_status` for that.

## Steps to reproduce
```bash
zeroclaw agent
# In the interactive session:
# 1) ask: what time is it
# 2) wait ~60 seconds
# 3) ask again: what time is it
```

## Impact
Affected users: anyone using long-lived interactive conversations.
Frequency: always.
Consequence: incorrect time-dependent answers (scheduling, log correlation, time references).

## Logs / stack traces
N/A

## ZeroClaw version
0.1.7 (released binary)

## Rust version
N/A (released binary; Rust toolchain not installed in this environment)

## Operating system
macOS 26.3 (25D125)

## Regression?
Unknown

## Pre-flight checks
- [x] I reproduced this on the latest main branch or latest release.
- [x] I redacted secrets/tokens from logs.
- [x] I removed personal identifiers and replaced identity-specific data with neutral placeholders.

expected: Each answer reflects the actual current time at that turn.
defect: The second answer repeats the time from session start because the system prompt's '## Current Date & Time' value is generated once and reused for later turns.

fault location.explanation: Renders the wall-clock time into the system prompt once; PR #2447 (commit 13790ac) adds refresh_prompt_datetime to rewrite this section on each turn.

Builds the system prompt only when history is empty and never updates it on later turns; PR #2447 adds an else-branch that refreshes the datetime of the existing system message (the same refresh is added in loop_.rs run, channels and gateway ws).

Root cause: FIXED UPSTREAM IN https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/2447 (commit https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/commit/13790ac2b911beda91e4c773323ea24105e951c2, "fix(agent): refresh system prompt datetime across long-lived turns"). In v0.1.7 the system prompt includes a DateTimeSection that formats Local::now() as "## Current Date & Time" when the prompt is built, and Agent::turn (and the interactive loop in loop_.rs) builds that system prompt only once, when history is empty. Later turns reuse the cached system message, so the model treats the start-of-session timestamp as authoritative and answers "what time is it" with a stale time. PR #2447 adds prompt::refresh_prompt_datetime, which rewrites the timestamp payload of the existing section, and calls it before each turn in Agent::turn, loop_::run, channel and websocket prompt builders. 13790ac first ships in v0.1.8, but it sits on a branch that is not an ancestor of the pinned revision; the pinned v0.8.5 solves the problem differently: DateTimeSection now renders the date and UTC offset without wall-clock time (crates/zeroclaw-runtime/src/agent/prompt.rs L465-471, test at L1049) and Agent prefixes every user message with a fresh `[CURRENT DATE & TIME: ...]` line (agent.rs L1046-1067). The defect is therefore not expected to reproduce at the pinned revision.
